rule_text: When a customer account inquiry is requested, the system looks up the account record; if no matching account is found, it displays an "ACCOUNT NOT FOUND" message and does not display any account details.
This account inquiry function is read-only: it only displays the current balance and status, and never updates account information.
When the account is found, the inquiry result displayed to the user includes the account identifier, the current account balance, and the account status.
Only Savings and Checking are recognized account types; any other account type is logged as a data exception but the account still continues through processing.
When an account's type is neither Savings nor Checking, the system displays a data exception message identifying the account, but does not stop processing it.
The number of days since an account's last transaction is calculated by comparing today's date to the account's last transaction date.
An active account with no transaction activity for more than 180 days is automatically reclassified as dormant.
A dormant account with no transaction activity for more than 365 days is automatically closed by the system.
For checking accounts, a fee code is assigned based on balance: accounts with a negative balance get an overdraft fee code, while accounts with a zero or positive balance get the standard fee code.

The fee code must only ever be set for checking accounts; savings accounts share the same stored data location for their interest rate, so setting a fee code on a savings account would corrupt its recorded interest rate.
The monthly maintenance fee is waived if the account balance is more than $500.00; if the balance is $500.00 or less, the fee is applied.
Monthly maintenance fee waiver checking is only performed for accounts that are currently active (not dormant or closed).
When a monthly maintenance fee is applied, it is deducted directly from the account's balance.
Every time a monthly maintenance fee is applied, a fee transaction record is created showing the account, the fee amount, the resulting balance, and the date.
The account record keeps a running count of days since the last transaction, updated each processing cycle.
At the end of each run, a control report is produced summarizing the total accounts processed, the number newly marked dormant, the number closed, and the number of monthly fees charged.
If the account number on the deposit cannot be found in the account file, the deposit is rejected.
A deposit is rejected if the account status is closed.
If the account is dormant (and not closed), a deposit automatically reactivates the account to active status.
The deposit amount is added to the account's current balance.
When a deposit is posted, the account's last-transaction date is updated to the current date.
If the account balance after the deposit is at or above the fee-waiver threshold, the monthly maintenance fee is waived for this account.
If the account balance after the deposit is below the fee-waiver threshold, a monthly maintenance fee is immediately deducted from the account balance.

Every accepted deposit is recorded as a transaction log entry showing the account number, a transaction type of deposit, the deposit amount, the resulting account balance, and the date of the transaction.
When a deposit is accepted, the account's stored record is updated to reflect the new balance and status.
If the account fails validation (not found or closed), no posting, fee check, or transaction logging occurs for that deposit.
Interest is only calculated for accounts that are both a savings account type and currently active; checking accounts, dormant accounts, and closed accounts are not eligible to earn interest.
If an eligible account's balance is $10,000.00 or more, the account earns a bonus annual interest rate of 4.5% instead of its normally stored interest rate.
If an eligible account's balance is below $10,000.00, the account earns interest at its individually stored interest rate rather than the bonus rate.
Monthly interest earned on an eligible account is calculated as the account's balance multiplied by its applicable annual interest rate, divided by 12, rounded to the nearest cent.
The calculated monthly interest is added to the account's balance, crediting the account.
When interest is posted to an account, the account's last transaction date is updated to the current processing date.

Each interest payment is recorded as a transaction history entry showing the account number, a transaction type of 'IN' (interest), the interest amount credited, the resulting account balance after posting, and the date of posting.
The account's master record is updated to reflect the new balance and last transaction date whenever interest is posted.
Each customer statement begins with a header line showing the account identifier and the current account balance.
A statement lists only the transactions that belong to the account currently being statemented (i.e., transactions are matched to the account by account ID).
Each listed transaction line on the statement shows the transaction type, the transaction amount, and the transaction date.

Whenever a statement is generated for an account, the account's last-activity date is updated to the current date, regardless of whether any customer transactions occurred during the statement period.
A withdrawal request is rejected if the account cannot be found.
A withdrawal is rejected if the account is closed or dormant; a dormant account must be reactivated with a deposit before a withdrawal can be made.
A withdrawal is rejected if completing it would drop the account balance below a required $100.00 overdraft cushion.
When a withdrawal is approved, the withdrawal amount is deducted from the account balance and the account's last transaction date is updated to the current date.

An approved withdrawal is recorded as a transaction record showing the account id, a transaction type of withdrawal, the withdrawal amount, the resulting account balance, and the transaction date, and the account's record is updated to reflect the new balance.
Every overdraft protection request is defaulted to "denied" and "no link" before processing begins, so that if processing fails partway through, the request is never mistakenly approved.
If an account has no overdraft protection linked to it, the overdraft request is denied immediately without ever checking an overdraft limit.
An overdraft request is approved only if the requested amount does not exceed the account's linked overdraft limit; otherwise it is denied.
The first use of overdraft protection by an account in a calendar month is free of charge.
Every overdraft protection use after the first one in the same calendar month incurs a flat fee.
Each time an overdraft fee is calculated and applied, the account's count of overdraft protection uses for the month is increased by one.
The response to an overdraft request always includes the approval decision and the fee amount, even when the fee is zero.
